Forbidden.description: Authenticated, but the credential may not act on this resource. Note: cross-TENANT access returns 404, not 403, so the API is not an existence oracle.

ApiKeyMetadata.description: Metadata view. The secret material exists only in the create response, once.

BackupStatus.description: Reports ONLY what the append-only backup ledger proves. A deployment with no ledger answers state=not_configured; this endpoint never asserts protection it cannot evidence.

encrypted.description: Whether every recorded backup was encrypted at rest. null = nothing recorded.

last_verified_restore.description: null = no restore has ever been verified.

offsite.description: Geographic redundancy, a SEPARATE axis from `protected`. `protected` answers "can this be restored, proven by drill"; this answers "would a copy survive losing this host".

includes_pitr.description: Whether the last successful sync also carried the base backups and WAL archive. False with PITR configured means point-in-time recovery does not survive losing this host.

pitr.description: Point-in-time recovery — the axis that decides how MUCH data a disaster costs, as opposed to whether anything can be recovered at all.

state.description: not_configured = no WAL archiving, so the recovery point is the dump interval. unverified = archiving runs but no point-in-time recovery has ever been proven.

rpo_basis.description: Which record the estimate came from. A failing or stale WAL archive is never used as the basis.

rpo_estimate_seconds.description: Worst-case data loss in seconds as evidenced by the ledger. null when nothing is recorded — an unknown RPO is reported as unknown, never as zero.

state.description: verified = a current backup AND a restore drill inside the quarterly window. unverified = backups run but no restore has ever been proven — an untested backup is an assumption, so this is NOT protected.

summary.description: One actionable sentence. Never contains a path, bucket, host or backup id.

CheckoutRequest.description: Client supplies only plan_code + idempotency, never amount/currency.

reference.description: Env var name or resource ARN — never secret value

CustodyProfile.description: Public custody metadata only — no private keys or credential values.

checksum_mismatches.description: Same version, different content. Never automatic to resolve.

pending_versions.description: Required by this build, not applied. Queries using them fail at request time.

state.description: `ahead` (database newer than the binary) is HEALTHY — that is the normal state during a rollback.

summary.description: One actionable sentence. Never contains a connection string or checksum bytes.

unknown_versions.description: Applied but unknown to this build.

current_daily_loss_ref.description: Reference-unit limit or null; see rules.

current_drawdown_ref.description: Reference-unit limit or null; see rules.

daily_loss_limit_ref.description: Reference-unit limit or null; see rules.

max_drawdown_limit_ref.description: Reference-unit limit or null; see rules.

SecuritySummary.description: Every field is derived from this deployment's configuration or from the credential that made the request. None of them is a constant.

audit_available.description: True only when the audit trail is DB-chained and therefore verifiable after a restart.

custody_mode.description: Read from [signing].provider. Only `local` is implemented; the others fail startup rather than falling back.

mfa_status.description: `not_supported` in every build that has no MFA implementation — stated plainly rather than as `unknown`, which would imply the capability might exist.

secret.description: Shown once during enrollment; never returned by status or device-list endpoints.

WalletBinding.description: A tenant's authorized wallet binding. Public address only — no signing material exists in the SaaS layer.

bearerAuth.description: A SaaS session token (login) or a tenant API key. The tenant context is the credential's own organization unless the caller is a platform administrator.

info.description: Multi-tenant SaaS contract over the TASK 7A control plane. Trading truth (orders, fills, positions, risk, ledger, HA) remains owned by the TASK 1–6 engines and is exposed read-only to tenants. Billing/usage reads are served through the deterministic exports (`/api/saas/exports?kind=subscription|usage|...`); there are no separate plan-catalogue or usage endpoints.
info.title: Sniper Suite SaaS Control Plane

Platform administrators only: the answer describes the deployment, not a tenant, and it exposes the shape of the schema. Production runs with DATABASE_AUTO_MIGRATE=false, so a binary can start, pass /health and /ready, and still be missing the columns its queries use — this endpoint is the only external way to see that. A database AHEAD of the binary is reported as healthy because that is the expected state during a rollback.

get.summary: Does the database schema match this build? 200 for in_sync or ahead, 503 for pending, dirty or checksum_mismatch.
